raw_response:
I am 71 years old, and I have farmed these fields for 50 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the labels on fertilizer bags and I have been to a few village training meetings, but honestly I do what has worked for me and what I see working in my neighbors' fields. I do not trust new ideas unless I saw them work on Lao Zhang's plot or the village demonstration field.

I have 12 mu total. Ten mu I keep in wheat-maize rotation, and two mu I plant with cotton. At my age, with just my husband and me, I cannot handle more cotton — the picking is too hard on my back, and hiring pickers costs 80 yuan per day plus meals.

For wheat, I use an improved variety. Last year I planted what my neighbor Lao Zhang used, and his wheat looked fuller than mine, so this year I am using the same seed from the same dealer. In October, after the rotary tiller goes through, I broadcast one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — on each mu as base fertilizer. I never skip this. At green-up time in March, I spread half a bag of urea per mu. Some people at the training said I could use less, but I would rather waste a little fertilizer than have yellow, thin wheat. A bag of urea is over 100 yuan now, and I feel the pain when I pay, but a bad harvest is a disaster — we live off this land. I irrigate three times from my well: before winter freeze, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. My well has enough water for three times, but I do not waste electricity. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for scab.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed immediately after cutting the wheat in early June. There is no time to plow; I use the no-till seeder from the machinery service, which costs 40 yuan per mu. At planting I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows. When the plants are knee-high, I side-dress half a bag of urea per mu. If the rain is good I irrigate twice, if it is dry I irrigate three times, but usually twice is enough in summer here. Pesticide twice — herbicide right at planting, and one spray for armyworm in July.

Cotton is on two mu. I plough that land deep in April because cotton likes loose soil and the roots need to go deep. I use hybrid Bt cotton seed. Base fertilizer is one bag of compound per mu. I top-dress twice with urea during flowering and boll stage, about 20 kilograms each time. Cotton bollworm is the big enemy here even with Bt seed, so I spray five times. I irrigate three times: seedling, flowering, and boll period. If the weather cooperates I hope to get about 200 jin of cotton per mu.

Every yuan counts. Spending more on fertilizer means less for medicine or for hiring help at harvest. But I learned this from my father and from 50 years of doing it: if you starve the crops, you starve yourself. I watch what others do, and I adjust a little, but I do not take big risks.
